newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil judge grants injunction against Banerj sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil judge grants injunction against Banerj sale.

text.p: A Brazilian judge has granted an injunction suspending Tuesday's privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, said a court official.
The injunction was granted by Rio state Judge Ronald Pietri at the request of a bank employees union, he said.

The union has questioned Banerj's tender documents regarding the bank's pension and payroll-related debts. Under the tender details, Rio de Janeiro state would assume all of Banerj's debts to its pension fund, which would be covered by a federal loan.
According to the court official, the judge has ordered Rio de Janeiro state to publish new tender details without the item concerning the debts being assumed by the state.
"The auction will be suspended until the government complies with the conditions of the injunction," he said.
Rio de Janeiro Finance Secretariat had no immediate comment on the injunction, said a spokeswoman for the Finance office.
Banerj, formally known as Banco Banerj SA, was slated to be privatized in a closed-envelope auction at 1400 local time/1700 GMT on Tuesday on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
But the sale of Banerj, the first Brazilian state bank due to be privatized, also depends on a Senate approval of the 2.9 billion real loan to cover the pension-related debts.
The state failed to sell the bank last year due to worries over its debts and the possibility of injunctions against the sale.
